principles: Keep the repair bounded and segment-aware
Retain honest role and commit provenance
drivers: Additional causal-prefix and mutant-oracle gaps found after B-6846

options.name: A: Port the bounded candidate and close the observed gaps
pros: Directly covers every known safe and unsafe case
cons: Requires careful extension of causal prefixes and mutant assertions

options.name: B: Exact B-bcae text allowlist
cons: Fails equivalent safe wording and hides the semantic boundary

options.name: C: Replace the classifier with broad text interpretation
cons: Expands scope, raises compatibility risk, and is unnecessary for the bounded witnesses

chosen: A: Port the bounded candidate and close the observed gaps
rationale: Option A preserves the proven test-first candidate while correcting the two concrete gaps identified by later review. It provides focused evidence without expanding the classifier into a new language subsystem.

preMortem.scenario: A causal synonym bypasses the later-link detector.
preMortem.trigger: Only the original consequence markers are recognized.
preMortem.consequence: A linked unsafe conclusion is admitted.
preMortem.mitigation: Add exact Accordingly, For that reason, and So fixtures to the all-role matrix.

preMortem.scenario: The broad mutant appears killed after only one witness escapes.
preMortem.trigger: A single outer assert stops the matrix at its first failure.
preMortem.mitigation: Invoke and assert the broad mutant separately for every role and every witness.

preMortem.scenario: The support Story blocks its own reviewers again.
preMortem.trigger: Frozen requirement metadata combines controlled concepts outside an accepted fixture wrapper.
preMortem.consequence: No review run identifier can be issued.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep titles and ordinary metadata neutral; place exact unsafe strings only in complete negative-fixture wrappers.
